finding: This board blocks AI-generated sites from exporting on the grounds that the exporter escapes their HTML — a bug that has since been fixed in code, so building this board would re-introduce a false blocker on a working feature.
evidence: Board copy 174:634: "AI-built pages store their content as raw HTML, and the exporter escapes it — so the file would open as visible markup rather than a rendered page. Publishing works; exporting does not." packages/editor/src/engine/export/ExportEngine.ts:956-975 documents the fix and ships it: "`contentFormat: \"html\"` means `content` is already markup. AI site generation stores whole generated sections that way and the canvas mounts them un-escaped, so escaping them here published every AI-generated site as visible angle brackets. Those are emitted as markup — but sanitized first" — implemented in `renderContent` at :963-970 via `sanitizeHTML(content)`. No `aiGenerated` flag exists on any Prisma model and no AI-export warning string exists in packages/editor/src or packages/dashboard.
recommend: Cut the board. If a residual caveat is still true, it needs re-deriving from the current exporter, not from the 2026 defect this board pictures.

finding: Export is drawn as a full settings screen with an eight-state machine, but the product ships it as a modal launched from a one-card settings stub — so the eight boards describe a surface that does not exist in either place it is drawn.
evidence: SettingsTab.tsx:728-740, the whole `case "export"`, renders a `bd-set-section` with an h3, one line of copy and a `<Button color="light" size="xs">Open exporter</Button>` that emits `EVENTS.UI_TOGGLE_EXPORTER`. The real UI is ExportModal mounted at packages/editor/src/editor/shell/StudioModals.tsx:166 as `<ModalContent size="lg">` (ExportModal.tsx:207), also reachable from the palette (engine/commands/defaultCommands.ts:441). ExportModal has three tabs ("preview"|"code"|"options", :31), a loading state (:375-383), a zipLoading button label (:330-334) and an error state (:385-393) — it has no idle/format-selected/done separation and no empty state. Board 639:2754 on page 1:3 draws Export as a screen too.
recommend: Decide once whether Export is a modal or a settings screen. If the modal stays, redraw one modal board with its three tabs and its four real states, and retire all eight 1:4 boards plus 639:2754.

finding: The export format list offers Vue and Next.js as ordinary selectable options, but both are unimplemented in code — a user who picks one has chosen a format the exporter cannot produce.

finding: The banner explains a limitation in implementation-schedule language — it tells the user about middleware that has not shipped, which is a fact about the team, not about their site.

finding: Designer rationale is drawn inside the artboard in the content column, where it is indistinguishable from product copy and would be built as such.

finding: The paywall banner says 'upgrade to edit' but the board contains no upgrade control — the only Pro gate on the page is a dead end.

finding: Every integration row carries an empty grey square where its logo should be, on a screen whose entire scannability depends on recognising the service at a glance.

finding: 'Expired key' and 'Failing' share one amber treatment, so a pixel that has stopped collecting data and a webhook that is retrying look equally urgent.

Underneath, the two are different: 'key rejected on last publish' is broken until a human re-keys it; '3 failed deliveries in 24h' is a delivery-log condition that may self-heal.

finding: The SEO score is a bare number with no breakdown and no action, so the one measurement on the screen tells a user they are at 82 without telling them what the missing 18 is.

finding: A domain can only be removed once it is verified — the four states where a user is most likely to want to abandon or correct a domain offer no way out of them.

finding: Every Domains board shows exactly one domain and no primary selector, so the multi-domain case the data model and the API both support has no design.

finding: No board shows the permission-denied case, although the shipping screen disables its domain controls for non-admins rather than hiding them — the state a viewer or editor actually sees is undrawn.
